title: Phased Hosted Surface PRD: Minimal Launch + Degraded Mode Rollout
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Overview:
This PRD specifies a phased launch for the unified hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) focusing on a minimal, production-safe API for the first cohort of customers. We prioritize correctness and predictable latency over broad feature completeness for the initial launch window. The launch will deliberately ship with a documented degraded-mode behavior set and explicit fallbacks to smaller model variants and cached results to preserve SLOs under load.

Goals (first phase):
- Provide a single, well-documented hosted endpoint for text generation (chat/completions), embeddings, and reranking with a consistent authentication and quota model.
- Ensure latency P99 <= 500ms for short chat (<=64 tokens) under baseline traffic; graceful degradation instead of outright failures for overload scenarios.
- Instrument token-level cost, latency, and quality telemetry for each route; expose initial dashboard tiles in Console.
- Ship a canary for 10% traffic and gated rollout to 100% with automatic rollback if regressions are detected.

Out-of-scope (phase 1):
- Multi-tenant per-route complex quota policies (deferred to phase 2).
- Native multimodal inputs (image/audio).
- Per-request fine-grained function/tool calling beyond a simple structured output contract.

API Surface (minimal):
- POST /v1/hosted/generate - supports mode query: chat | completion.
- POST /v1/hosted/embeddings - returns single or batched vectors; batch size capped at 64.
- POST /v1/hosted/rerank - accepts N documents + query, returns score-ordered ids.
- Common: Bearer token auth, x-region header optional, url param "model_variant" allowed for advanced users.

Behavioral Contracts and Degraded Modes:
- If runtime detects model memory pressure, request is routed to a smaller quantized variant (documented mapping). Response includes header X-Model-Fallback: true and reason codes.
- If KV-cache hit returns value, response includes X-Cache: hit to aid debugging and charge visibility.
- For heavy requests exceeding batching windows, requests will be queued up to 250ms before forced fallback; queueing metrics emitted as queue_ms.

Telemetry and Observability:
- Required telemetry tags: route, model_variant, org_id, request_length_tokens, response_length_tokens, kv_cache_hit, fallback_reason, batch_id.
- Dashboards: per-route P50/P95/P99 latency, token cost per route, failed requests by error type, quality drift alerts (baseline evals).

Rollout Plan:
- Canary (10%) for internal customers and opt-in partners (1 week).
- Staged increase to 50% with 48h observation windows and evaluation against baseline traffic patterns (2 weeks).
- Full rollout after quality and SLO gates pass; ability to force regional rollback.

Trade-offs considered: 
- We intentionally limit batch sizes and disable some aggressive batching heuristics in phase 1 to keep tail latency bounds predictable. This increases cost per-token moderately but reduces P99 variance.
- Prefix caching scope narrowed to common system prompts and not arbitrary user prompt caching to limit cache correctness risk.

Decision log (partial):
- Agreed to expose model_variant parameter now rather than hide it: allows platform customers to opt into lower-cost variants under guidance (Decision: 2026-02-20, PM + Eng).
- Deferred quota per-route complexity to phase 2 to prevent launch delays (Decision: 2026-02-24).

Acceptance criteria (see separate field for checklist).

Open questions and next steps:
- Finalize per-request headers format for fallback reasons (ENG-3042).
- Confirm Console dashboard tile quotas and retention with Observability team (PM follow-up).
- Security review scheduling (security_review_required flagged).
